questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, you should look:

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: When using a freeway exit ramp, you should:

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until after you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Curve ahead.
Turn right or left.
Traffic moves only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign means traffic moves only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, you must pull over to the right side as far as safely possible and stop for emergency vehicles using lights and/or sirens. Do not stop inside an intersection.

questions.question: When you see reduced visibility, your first action should be:

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slowing down is your first response to poor visibility and dangerous conditions.

questions.question: A solid red arrow in a traffic signal:

options.text: Is never used as a traffic signal.
Means the same thing as a red circular light.
Means drivers may turn in the direction of the arrow.
Means traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means the same thing as a red circular light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a circular red light. Traffic in that lane must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb:

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your car will roll toward the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, you should:

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb to keep your car from rolling into traffic. If there is no curb, turn the wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: To check your blind spots before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help you drive safely at night?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly into oncoming headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into oncoming headlights.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights makes your eyes adjust. After the car passes, your eyes need time to readjust to the darker light. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle symbol is a reflective orange triangle. These vehicles drive at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: Signs that require drivers to follow a command are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: A designated no passing zone
A one-way traffic area
The blind spot of a large vehicle
An area designated for motor vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle
questions.explanation: "No zones" are large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles. Stay out of these areas when driving near large vehicles.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are more difficult to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more difficult to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away they are and how fast they are going. Always watch carefully for motorcycles.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic lanes moving toward each other.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Regardless of your direction.
Only if it is following you.
Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regardless of your direction.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. Do this whether it is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: What do round signs warn you about?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn of a railroad crossing ahead. Be extra careful when you see this sign.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as the traffic flow.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road where you can see traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Your headlights may be out of line if one side of your car is higher than the other.
You may damage a tire by driving onto the shoulder.
You may hydroplane if the shoulder is wet.
You may lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road. If you drift onto the shoulder, do not brake hard or turn sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.
